canonical_data: a Postgres session tape, scope-owned memory, files, skills, and cron records, with sandbox disks treated as disposable
current_repo_note: Covers the open QM core, CLI, and plugins. The third-party hosted version the README mentions is a separate offering.
strengths: Identity, scope, grants, and delivery are meant to be enforced by the core rather than trusted to the model or the sandbox, with each person and room holding separate memory, files, crons, and a durable sandbox
An organization picks a strict, auto, or dangerous tool-approval posture that narrower scopes can only tighten, and a predeclared command policy denies destructive commands in every posture
Work is driven from a central write-ahead session tape and run queue, so turns are meant to survive interruption, and the harness and model are swappable
weaknesses: Its own security policy calls it early, experimental software and says it is not a hardened public or multi-tenant service boundary
Contributions are accepted only as human-written proposal text, so the maintainers implement all code changes
Content screening is off by default, and the dangerous posture removes tool approval gates
Deployment needs a cloud account, Postgres, and sandbox provider setup rather than a single install
why_it_matters: An open implementation of an agent runtime designed for a whole company, where per-scope isolation and explicit grants replace one assistant per person.
